hero: A provincial hospital pediatric ward in Central Luzon at night: a Filipino mother sits on the bed holding her 7-month-old son with an intravenous line taped to his hand, while a pediatric nephrologist in a white coat kneels beside them and sketches a simple bladder and two kidneys on a notepad; a father appears on a phone video call held by the mother. Warm, calm light, no text.

figures.teaches: Infection needs a failed defense: a short ureteric tunnel, incomplete voiding or a full rectum, and reflux is graded I to V.
figures.content: Left panel: child's urinary tract with labels 'Kidney', 'Ureter', 'Bladder', 'Rectum'. Inset of bladder wall showing oblique ureteric tunnel labeled 'Flap-valve tunnel' (normal) and short tunnel labeled 'Short tunnel: reflux'. Arrows down the ureter labeled 'Urine washout'; arrow showing urine going back up labeled 'Reflux on voiding'. Full rectum pressing bladder labeled 'Constipation compresses bladder'. Right panel: five small kidney-ureter icons labeled 'Grade I' to 'Grade V' with increasing dilatation; caption under Grade IV-V 'High grade'. No numbers other than the grades.

figures.teaches: Confirm a UTI with a proper specimen, image on purpose, and decide on prophylaxis with absolute numbers.
figures.content: Boxes top to bottom: 'Febrile infant' -> 'Catheter or SPA urine' -> 'Pyuria + 50,000 CFU/mL' -> 'Renal-bladder ultrasound' -> branch 'Normal: no routine VCUG' / 'Abnormal or recurrence: VCUG'. Then 'Decide with family' with three options 'Prophylaxis', 'Urology referral', 'Observe, culture every fever'. Side card 'RIVUR: 39/302 vs 72/305 recurrences; scars 11.9% vs 10.2%'. Side card 'PREDICT: 21.2% vs 35.6%; NNT 7 over 2 years'. Bottom bar 'Treat bladder and bowel'.

card: A Filipino mother cradling an infant on a hospital bed while a doctor draws a simple kidney and bladder sketch for her.
